design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (late closing: buyer delay per diem -> buyer-signed closing extension).

[Why a good test] The buyer asks only to move a missed closing date. The charter makes the extension's counting day depend on buyer-delay per diem already standing on the ledger, so a careful agent must (1) read the extension rule's prerequisite sentence, (2) see in the ledger that no closing delay per diem stands although the scheduled closing date 2026-09-17 passed 20 days ago, (3) work out that only the per diem rule books such a charge, (4) compute that per diem through five factors (delay start, delay end, grace, studio-options rate, deposit-cover rate) over ledger history plus the buyer's Design Studio file, and only then (5) compute the extension length through four factors (counting day, financing base length read from the buyer's withdrawn Calloway Home Mortgage lock, construction-slip courtesy days, weekend roll) and hand the addendum to the buyer. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ledger rows and cross-product records, and arithmetic, not from tool choice: one write tool per problem.

[Scope snapshot] Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,4]; per diem took 5 factors, extension took 4. Occupied before: nothing. Claimed: purchase_ext_closing_delay_per_diem (assess_closing_delay_per_diem_8d15ee11, agent) and purchase_ext_buyer_closing_extension (sign_closing_extension_addendum_c0ddd0a3, user). Left for task 1 (draw prereq=1, factors [6,4]): the deposit side of the charter (purchase_deposit_posted under the returned-payment cure window, reservation transfers), untouched here.

[Problem-tree card] root = purchase_ext_buyer_closing_extension (customer's surface request). Edge root -> purchase_ext_closing_delay_per_diem: kind value_input, gate binding last_charged_offset (feeds start_offset), form state. Prerequisite sentence (in the extension rule, affirmative direction "only after"): "Where the buyer asks for the extension after the scheduled closing date has passed, the new closing date is set only after the ledger carries closing delay per diem for every day of buyer delay before the extension request was received." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; waited-on side is a record-visible state (closing delay per diem charges on the ledger); no tool/policy id/snake_case token; scope matches the condition (every buyer-delay day before the request). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a closing_delay_per_diem charge: the per diem policy's tool (the extension tool moves a date; task 1's tools post deposits). Derivation: sentence + ledger (only one purchase_charge_assessed row, charge_type closing_extension_fee CHG-HP-2341 dated 2026-10-05; no per diem row) + the per diem rule ("booked as one closing delay per diem charge that records the period's first day and last day") -> the one resolving action is booking the per diem. Unmet at opening: initial_state.purchase_events holds no row with charge_type closing_delay_per_diem; purchase_agreements.buyer_charges_due = 1500.00 equals the extension fee alone. Resolver owner: agent. Topological order: per diem (step 8) then extension (step 10). Deletion sensitivity (verify.py run): skipping the per diem write leaves perdiem_count=0, so start_offset falls to 0 and extension_days = 28 instead of 46; terminal per diem row also missing. The persona never names per diem or delay charges; it reacts only after the agent explains them. The tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] Per diem subject purchase_charge_assessed is governed by purchase_closing_schedule, purchase_plan_lot_changes, purchase_returned_payment, purchase_cancellation_refund; none has an eligibility gate applying to purchase_charge_assessed (policy_scope each). Scope facts: status closing_scheduled (agreement row), buyer-side delay (buyer's own lender, persona + financing_type outside_lender). Overwrite declared: base clause "a closing_delay_per_diem of per_diem_usd per calendar day accrues from the day after per_diem_grace_days have elapsed, booked as one charge per delay period with its first and last day" is replaced by the extended period/grace/rate rules. Extension subject purchase_closing_extended: purchase_closing_schedule gate extension_state ("A closing extension is written only on an agreement whose status is closing_scheduled.") holds: initial_state.purchase_agreements.<A>.status = closing_scheduled; purchase_builder_delay applies only through policy_scope (its gate concerns cancellations). Overwrite declared on "each extension adds closing_extension_days calendar days to the current scheduled closing date". No time gates on either subject. closing_extensions_used 0 < closing_extension_max 2 for Summit.

[Business-object card] Target: Home Purchase Agreement <A> (Summit Collection, LM-0236, contract 812,990.00). Per diem aggregates only this agreement's purchase_events (scoped by purchase_id). Deposits held for the cover factor: deposit_posted 40,649.50 (initial EM, RCPT-HP-21437) + 24,389.70 (additional, RCPT-HP-22918) + 40,649.50 (outside-lender extra, RCPT-HP-24063) = 105,688.70; no refunds/forfeitures/returns -> 13.0% of contract price. Excluded from deposits: incentive grants (20,000 + 10,000) and their revocations on 2026-08-26 (incentive_credit account, not earnest money) — near-miss for the cover factor. Extension request evidence: the 2026-10-05 closing extension fee charge (already booked when the emailed request was received; no fee write is owed in this task). Cross-product objects: Design Studio file <D> (Studio Signature, finalized, option_total 68,450.00); rate lock <L> (180-Day Extended Lock, withdrawn 2026-08-26, fee 3,251.96 forfeited with reason buyer_withdrawal).

[Factor card — per diem, expected 1782.00, all-baseline 3825.00]
- delay_start (method): estimated completion 2026-09-10 is before the scheduled date (completion_offset -7) and the latest closing date notice (2026-08-10) gave 38 days < closing_notice_days 45 -> period starts the day after 2026-09-24, i.e. 2026-09-25 (offset 8). Baseline (day after scheduled date, 2026-09-18) -> 3168.00.
- delay_end (method): extension fee charge dated 2026-10-05 (after 2026-09-17) -> period ends 2026-10-04 (offset 17). Baseline (day before booking date, 2026-10-06) -> 2178.00.
- request_grace (parameter): exactly one closing extension fee charge -> one day fewer than per_diem_grace_days (2 - 1 = 1 grace day). Baseline per_diem_grace_days 2 -> 1584.00.
- studio_options_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty design; status and option total are two fields of one design row, so it is not counted as multi-source — the task's multi-source factor is financing_base_length, agreement financing_type AND the lock row): file finalized and option total 68,450 >= 40,000 and < 75,000 -> multiplier 1.10. Near-miss: a reader who adds removed/credited studio money or uses deposits would cross 75,000. Baseline 1 -> 1620.00.
- deposit_cover_rate (parameter): deposits held 13.0% >= 12% -> 0.80. Baseline 1 -> 2227.50.
Computation: period 2026-09-25..2026-10-04 = 10 days, less 1 grace day = 9 billed days; daily rate RND(225 x 1.10 x 0.80) = 198.00; 9 x 198.00 = 1782.00.
[Factor card — extension, expected 46, all-baseline 14]
- extension_counting_day (method, multi-source): per diem booked through 2026-10-04 -> counts from offset 17. Baseline (scheduled date) -> 28.
- financing_base_length (parameter, cross-difficulty lock): financing outside_lender and a withdrawn Calloway Home Mortgage lock exists -> 21 days. Baseline closing_extension_days 14 -> 39.
- construction_slip_courtesy (parameter): completion 2026-09-10 is 13 days after contract completion 2026-08-28 (<= 21) -> 7 courtesy days. Baseline 0 -> 39.
- weekend_closing_roll (method, nearest weekday: Saturday back to the Friday before, Sunday forward to the Monday after, weekday unchanged — three distinct methods): 17+21+7 = 45 -> 2026-11-01, a Sunday -> forward to Monday 2026-11-02, 46. Baseline (no roll) -> 45.

[Seed rows] customer (identity); agreement (status, dates, financing, cache balances consistent with ledger: earnest_money_held 105,688.70 = deposits; buyer_charges_due 1,500.00 = fee; incentive_balance 0 = 30,000 granted - 30,000 revoked); 9 ledger rows (history for cover factor, notice for delay_start, fee charge for delay_end/grace); design file (cross rate factor); lock + 2 lock ledger rows (withdrawal evidence for base length; fee paid/forfeited as the lock charter requires). Automatic clauses checked: no buyer delay beyond max_buyer_delay_days 45 (purchase_msr_buyer_delay_days runs through the frozen date: 20 days) so no default notice is owed; financing change already carried its revocations and outside-lender deposit; lock withdrawal already carried its fee forfeiture. No row is read only as noise; every row enters gold reads.

[Persona design] Calm, slightly embarrassed pharmacist; volunteers only the surface goal (push my closing date back), the emailed request and the visible portal facts (fee, unsigned addendum). Identity and financing facts only on request. No standing pre-authorisation of charges in the opening (removed in round 2). Passive reactions: accepts a late-days charge only once the representative explains it; signs the addendum when handed over; ends after hearing the new date. No template labels; no prerequisite hint.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (ssn_last4 + ZIP) -> agreement -> ledger -> design file -> rate lock -> lock ledger -> unlock + call per diem (2026-09-25..2026-10-04, 1782.00) -> unlock_user + buyer calls the addendum tool (extension_days 46; new date 2026-11-02).

[Verification code] _author/verify.py (authoring scratch, removed at hand-off) replays gold writes with the real tools up to each computation's step and evaluates the policy compute with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute; output: per diem result 1782.0, factor baselines {delay_start 3168.0, delay_end 2178.0, request_grace 1584.0, studio_options_rate 1620.0, deposit_cover_rate 2227.5}, all-baseline 3825.0; extension result 46, factor baselines {extension_counting_day 28, financing_base_length 39, construction_slip_courtesy 39, weekend_closing_roll 45}, all-baseline 14; skip per diem -> extension 28. Gates: see solvability/closure fields and the difficulty worklog.

[Rule <-> compute two-way sweep] Every ladder binding quotes its full ladder sentence in compute_basis; the reverse sweep claims every rule sentence carrying a window (period first/last day, both included), filter (closing_delay_per_diem / closing_extension_fee charges, deposit event types), branch (each ladder), cap (billed days never below zero via MX) and rounding (daily rate rounded once, result rounded to the cent). The weekend roll is stated as Saturday -> Friday before (-1) / Sunday -> Monday after (+1) and computed from a known Monday reference.

[Visible-context draft recomputation] From the rules, the ledger rows the finders return and the persona alone: the extension rule's sentence forces per diem first; per diem rule gives 2026-09-25 start (short notice), 2026-10-04 end (fee date), 1 grace day, rate 225 x 1.10 x 0.80 = 198.00, 9 billed days, 1782.00; extension counts from 2026-10-04, 21 + 7 days -> Sunday 2026-11-01 -> 2026-11-02, 46 days from 2026-09-17. Agrees with gold.

[Round-2 rework log (audit audits/policy_task/purchase_deposits_and_closing)]
- T0-F1 / charter F1: weekend_closing_roll's Saturday and Sunday tiers selected one method (roll to Monday). Rule, compute and ladder now move a weekend date to the nearest weekday: Saturday back to the Friday before, Sunday forward to the Monday after, weekday unchanged. This world takes the Sunday tier; extension_days and every factor figure unchanged (46; baseline 45). P2 keeps 4 real factors.
- T0-F2: removed the opening's unconditional "happy for the representative to put on your agreement whatever your contract says you owe"; the only reaction to charges is the conditional one, triggered when the representative explains a late-days charge (T0-O1 wording "days since September 17" replaced by "days you were late past your closing date").
- T0-O2: the rationale no longer calls studio_options_rate multi-source. T0-O3: delay-measure figure corrected to 20 days.
- Charter F3 (grace ladder): the one-request tier is now per_diem_grace_days less one day, never below zero (the separate 1-day parameter is gone), so a request never yields more grace than no request; on this Summit world 2 - 1 = 1, unchanged. Charter F4: P2 tier-2 compute now also requires that no per diem has been charged. Neither changes a figure on this world (re-verified by check_compute).
user_scenario:
You are Nadia Hartwell, a hospital pharmacist buying a new Summit Collection home, The Kestrel Ridge - Elevation C on lot LM-0236 in Larkspur Meadows, Castle Rock, Colorado. You are calm and organised but a little embarrassed, because your closing on September 17 came and went: in late August you moved your mortgage from Calloway Home Mortgage to Front Range Credit Union, and the credit union's underwriting has been slower than promised. You open by saying you need to push my closing date back, that you emailed the Homebuyer desk on Monday, October 5 asking for an extension, and that your buyer portal now shows a $1,500 extension fee and an extension addendum waiting for your signature with the new closing date left blank. You want the new closing date set today so you can sign the addendum yourself.

You give your details only when the representative asks for them, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 303-555-0127 (3035550127), the last four of your Social Security number are 3318, your mailing ZIP code is 80104, your date of birth is March 14, 1986, and your email is nadia.hartwell@outlook.com. Your mailing address is 2246 Briar Glen Lane, Castle Rock, CO 80104. You do not know any reference numbers for your agreement and expect the representative to look it up.

If the representative asks about your financing, you confirm that you withdrew your Calloway Home Mortgage rate lock in late August and are now borrowing through Front Range Credit Union; if asked when the credit union can fund, you say they have told you the very end of October, and any closing date after that suits you. You know your design selections were finished in the studio over the summer but you do not remember the totals. You have no other open agreement with Calloway and no other request today.

You have not thought about any other charges. Only if the representative explains that a charge has to be posted to your agreement for days you were late past your closing date do you react: you sigh, say you half expected that, and tell them to go ahead. If they tell you an amount, you accept it without arguing. When the representative tells you the extension addendum is ready for you to sign, you sign it yourself with the details they give you, and you read back the new closing date it shows. Once you have heard the new closing date, you thank them, say you will forward it to your loan officer, and end the call. You never suggest how anything should be calculated and never ask for any change to the amounts.
